findings.who: A shareholder whose only S corporation loss is a box 9 net section 1231 loss (for example, a loss on disposition of business assets), with no loss in boxes 1, 2, 3, 7, or 8a, and who has stock or loan basis that is not at risk.
findings.why_no: The gate counts only losses in boxes 1, 2, 3, 7 and 8a; a box 9 loss makes the computed condition false, so the not-at-risk question is skipped even though the IRS at-risk text expressly includes a loss on disposition of assets.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 3: 'These losses and deductions include a loss on the disposition of assets and the section 179 expense deduction.'
findings.fix: Add box 9 to the gate, or gate on any activity loss or other deduction subject to the at-risk rules, not only the enumerated boxes.

findings.who: A shareholder with a box 10 other loss from the S corporation's trade or business or income-producing activity, no loss in boxes 1, 2, 3, 7, or 8a, and amounts not at risk.
findings.why_no: Box 10 is omitted from the gate, so a box 10 loss is treated as no loss and the not-at-risk question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 3: 'if you have (a) a loss or other deduction from any activity carried on as a trade or business or for the production of income by the corporation, and (b) amounts in the activity for which you aren't at risk, you will have to complete Form 6198'
findings.fix: Include box 10 losses or gate on any activity loss or deduction subject to at-risk.

findings.who: A shareholder with a section 179 expense deduction in box 11 (or another at-risk other deduction in box 12) and no loss in boxes 1, 2, 3, 7, or 8a, who has not-at-risk stock or loan basis.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only for a loss in the listed boxes; a section 179 or other deduction is not a loss in those boxes, so the filer is not asked even though the at-risk rules limit the deduction.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 3: 'These losses and deductions include a loss on the disposition of assets and the section 179 expense deduction'; and the general rule applies to a 'loss or other deduction from any activity' when amounts are not at risk.
findings.fix: Ask the not-at-risk question when box 11 section 179 (or another at-risk deduction) is present, even if the listed loss boxes are zero.

findings.who: A shareholder with two activities in one S corporation: one activity has a loss and not-at-risk amounts, while another activity has enough income that the K-1 box (for example, box 1) shows no net loss.
findings.why_no: The gate tests the net box total, not each activity; the filer truthfully sees no loss in the box and is not asked, but at-risk limits apply activity by activity.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 3: 'Since at-risk limitations apply for each activity, you should get a separate statement of income, expenses, and other items for each activity from the corporation.'
findings.fix: Use the separate activity statement and gate on any activity-level loss subject to at-risk, not on the net K-1 box.

findings.who: A shareholder with a prior-year section 465 loss suspended by the at-risk rules from this S corporation, and no current-year loss in boxes 1, 2, 3, 7, or 8a, whose current at-risk amount determines whether and how much of the carryover is allowed.
findings.why_no: The gate looks only for a current-year loss in the listed boxes; with current income or no current loss, the filer is not asked, even though the prior-year suspended loss makes current at-risk status matter.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 3: 'Any loss from a section 465 activity not allowed for this tax year will be treated as a deduction allocable to the activity in the next tax year.'
findings.fix: Include prior-year suspended at-risk losses from this S corporation or activity in the gate, or ask about carryovers separately.

findings.who: On a joint return, the taxpayer-spouse does not own the S corporation, but the other spouse does and has stock or loan basis that is not at risk.
findings.why_no: The gated question says 'you' and asks what 'you put into it'; the taxpayer can truthfully answer no for himself or herself, leaving out the spouse's facts that make the joint return's line true.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 3: 'if you have (a) a loss or other deduction from any activity ... and (b) amounts in the activity for which you aren't at risk, you will have to complete Form 6198'
findings.fix: Ask 'you or your spouse' and include the spouse's S corporation interests and at-risk amounts on a joint return.

findings.who: A shareholder who borrowed money to invest in the S corporation from a fellow shareholder, or from a relative of a shareholder, and must repay the loan personally.
findings.why_no: The help says 'A bank loan you must repay yourself does not count'; the filer reads that as any loan they must repay, even though a loan from a person with an interest in the activity (other than an ordinary creditor) is not at risk under the IRS rule.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 3: not at risk when the stock or loan basis is from a source 'covered by indebtedness from a person who has an interest in the activity or from a person related to a person (except you) having such an interest, other than a creditor.'
findings.fix: Clarify that the bank-loan exception is only for ordinary creditors and that loans from owners, persons with an interest, or their relatives are not at risk even if the filer is personally liable.

locators: p. 3, At-Risk Limitations, "you will have to complete Form 6198, At-Risk Limitations, to figure your allowable loss for the activity"

findings.who: A shareholder who personally did no work in the S corporation in 2025, but whose spouse did substantially all the participation or enough significant-participation hours so the shareholder is treated as materially participating.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'you' worked in the business; the filer truthfully says no because the spouse did the work, even though the gated question itself asks 'you (or your spouse)'.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through an S corporation ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Make the gate 'Did you or your spouse work in the business during the corporation's tax year?' and compute tests 1, 3, 5, and 6 using the spouse's work.

findings.who: A shareholder in an S corporation with a fiscal tax year ending in 2025 who performed substantially all participation during the part of the corporation's tax year falling in 2024, but did no work in calendar 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'in 2025'; the filer reads that as calendar 2025 and answers no, even though the work was in the corporation's tax year.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'All determinations of material participation are based on your participation during the corporation’s tax year.'
findings.fix: Replace 'in 2025' with 'during the corporation's tax year' and use the K-1 tax year, not the calendar year.

findings.who: A shareholder whose S corporation activity produced no box 1 ordinary income (box 1 zero or blank) but had a separately stated rental real estate loss or passive credit, and who materially participated in that activity under test 2, 4, or 7.
findings.why_no: The first helper is false whenever box 1 shows no amount, so the tool never asks; the filer never gets to say yes to material participation that matters for the rental loss or credit.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the corporation; and (b) if you were a real estate professional, in each rental real estate activity held through the corporation.'
findings.fix: Remove the box-1-only gate; ask when any K-1 activity has a loss, credit, or other item affected by passive activity rules, not only when box 1 has an amount.

findings.who: A shareholder who performed about 80-85% of all participation in the S corporation activity, with the rest done by employees, which can be 'substantially all' under the IRS standard but is not naturally described as 'almost all'.
findings.why_no: The gated question asks 'do almost all its work'; the filer reads that as requiring near-total work and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4, test 2: 'Your participation in the activity for the tax year constituted substantially all the participation in the activity of all individuals (including individuals who aren’t owners of interests in the activity).'
findings.fix: Ask whether participation constituted 'substantially all the participation in the activity of all individuals, including non-owners' instead of 'almost all its work'.

findings.who: A shareholder with more than 100 hours in this S corporation and more than 500 hours total in significant participation activities, where the additional hours are in a partnership or sole proprietorship rather than another S corporation.
findings.why_no: The question says 'over 500 hours in all such businesses'; the filer reads 'such businesses' as other S corporations or similar corporations, not all significant participation activities including activities outside the corporation.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4, test 4: 'The activity was a significant participation activity for the tax year, and you participated in all significant participation activities (including activities outside the corporation) during the year for more than 500 hours.'
findings.fix: Say 'all significant participation activities, including activities outside this corporation' and define significant participation activity as more than 100 hours with no material participation under another test.

findings.who: A shareholder who participated on a regular, continuous, and substantial basis (test 7) but did not do almost all the work and did not have 100/500 hours, and who does not recognize facts-and-circumstances as a listed material participation test.
findings.why_no: The question lists 'almost all', '100/500', or 'another material participation test'; the filer reads the specifics as the whole rule and does not know that regular, continuous, substantial participation is itself a test.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4, test 7: 'Based on all the facts and circumstances, you participated in the activity on a regular, continuous, and substantial basis during the tax year.'
findings.fix: Spell out the facts-and-circumstances test in the question or help, or ask a broad yes/no about regular, continuous, substantial participation and classify after.

findings.who: A shareholder who is a retired or disabled farmer, or the surviving spouse of a farmer, and is treated as materially participating under the special rules but did not work in the business in 2025 and meets none of tests 1, 3, 5, or 6.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether they worked in the business and whether no test is met; they truthfully answer that they did not work and do not meet the listed tests, so the special-rule participation is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'Special rules apply to certain retired or disabled farmers and to the surviving spouses of farmers. See Instructions for Form 8582 for details.'
findings.fix: Add a gate or question for the retired-or-disabled-farmer and surviving-spouse special rules, or state that they are treated as materially participating without meeting tests 1-7.

findings.who: A shareholder who worked in the S corporation in 5 of the prior 10 years but did not legally 'materially participate' in those years, and who meets test 2 or 4 in the current year; they answer the earlier-years helper yes because they were involved.
findings.why_no: The earlier-years helper asks the legal conclusion 'materially participated'; the filer reads it as 'worked/owned' and says yes, making the gate false and skipping the current-year other tests.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4, test 5: 'You materially participated in the activity for any 5 tax years (whether or not consecutive) during the 10 tax years that immediately precede the tax year'; test 2: 'substantially all the participation ...'
findings.fix: Ask checkable prior-year facts such as hours or participation, or do not let an uncertain prior-year answer suppress the current-year other-test question; ask current-year tests first.

locators: p. 4, Individuals, "Your participation in the activity for the tax year constituted substantially all the participation in the activity of all individuals"; "The activity was a significant participation activity for the tax year, and you participated in all significant participation activities (including activities outside the corporation) during the year for more than 500 hours"

p. 4, Material participation, "Material participation standards for shareholders who are individuals are listed below"; p. 4, Individuals, "You participated in the activity for more than 500 hours during the tax year"

findings.who: A shareholder in an S corporation with two trade or business activities identified on the K-1 statement: Activity A in which the shareholder worked more than 500 hours in 2025, and Activity B in which the shareholder did not meet test 1 or test 3 in 2025 but did materially participate in Activity B in 5 of 2015-2024.
findings.why_no: The tool computes the gate once for the whole S corporation. Because Activity A meets test 1, the gate is false and the earlier-years question is never asked for Activity B, so Activity B's prior material participation is dropped.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: "You must determine if you materially participated ... in each trade or business activity held through the corporation"; "You materially participated in the activity for any 5 tax years ... during the 10 tax years that immediately precede the tax year."
findings.fix: Compute test 1/3 and ask the earlier-years question separately for each activity identified on the K-1 statement; one activity's current-year test 1/3 should not suppress another activity's test 5/6.

findings.who: A real estate professional shareholder in an S corporation whose only S-corporation activity is rental real estate reported in Box 2, with Box 1 zero; the shareholder materially participated in that rental activity in 5 of 2015-2024 but does not meet test 1 or test 3 in 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate requires Box 1 to show an amount. With only Box 2 rental income, the tool treats the gate as false and never asks the earlier-years question, even though prior material participation in the rental activity matters.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: "Passive activities don’t include ... Rental real estate activities in which you materially participated if you were a real estate professional for the tax year"; "if you were a real estate professional ... in each rental real estate activity held through the corporation."
findings.fix: Gate on any S-corporation activity with income, loss, or credit, including Box 2/3 rental real estate activities when the filer is a real estate professional, and ask per activity.

findings.who: A filer who materially participated in a personal-service S corporation activity in 2012, 2013, and 2014, but not in 2015-2024, and does not meet test 1 or test 3 in 2025.
findings.why_no: The question reads as if the personal-service alternative is limited to 3 years within the listed 2015-2024 range. The filer answers no because they have no qualifying years in that window.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: "The activity was a personal service activity and you materially participated in the activity for any 3 tax years (whether or not consecutive) preceding the tax year."
findings.fix: For personal-service activities, say 'any 3 tax years before the current year, not limited to 2015-2024' and make clear the 10-year range applies only to the 5-year test.

findings.who: A filer who materially participated more than 500 hours in 2016-2020, but the S corporation reported losses or no income in those years on Schedule E; the filer answers no because the help says a year counts only if 'its income' was in columns (i) or (k).
findings.why_no: They read 'income' literally and do not count loss or zero-income years, even though material participation is not conditioned on having income in the year.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: "You materially participated in the activity for any 5 tax years (whether or not consecutive) during the 10 tax years that immediately precede the tax year."
findings.fix: Remove the income-column limitation or state that a year counts if the activity was reported (income or loss) and the filer met a material participation test; material participation can exist in a loss year.

locators: p. 4, Individuals, "You materially participated in the activity for any 5 tax years (whether or not consecutive) during the 10 tax years that immediately precede the tax year"; "The activity was a personal service activity and you materially participated in the activity for any 3 tax years (whether or not consecutive) preceding the tax year"

p. 4, Material participation, "Material participation standards for shareholders who are individuals are listed below"; p. 4, Individuals, "You participated in the activity for more than 500 hours during the tax year"

findings.who: A couple files jointly for 2025 but filed separately for 2024, or married during 2025. The spouse owns the S corporation shares, and the spouse's own 2024 Form 8582 shows an unallowed loss for it in Part VII, column (c).
findings.why_no: The gate asks about 'your 2024 return' and 'your 2024 Form 8582'. The filer completing the return truthfully says their own 2024 return held back nothing, even though the spouse's 2024 return did.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV/Part V Column (c): "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Ask: "Does your 2024 Form 8582, or your spouse's 2024 Form 8582 (including one filed with a separate 2024 return), show an unallowed loss for this corporation in Part VII, column (c)?"

findings.who: A shareholder's passive loss from this corporation was disallowed in 2021 or 2022 and has been carried forward ever since. In 2024 the corporation had income, or its loss was allowed, but part of the old carryover is still listed in Part VII, column (c) of the 2024 Form 8582.
findings.why_no: The words 'Was a loss ... held back on your 2024 return' read as asking about a 2024 loss. The filer thinks the loss was held back in 2021, or that the corporation had no 2024 loss, and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Ask: "Does your 2024 Form 8582, Part VII, column (c), show any amount for this corporation? Include losses from any earlier year that are still carried forward, even if the corporation had income in 2024."

findings.who: A shareholder has suspended passive losses from an S corporation that issued no 2025 Schedule K-1. For example, the corporation was dormant but not disposed of, or it revoked its S election and became a C corporation.
findings.why_no: The gate is reached only inside a 2025 K-1 entry ('For this S corporation'). With no K-1 to enter, the filer never reaches the question, and the carryover listed on the 2024 Form 8582 is dropped.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Column (c): "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Add a per-return gate outside the K-1 documents: "Does your (or your spouse's) 2024 Form 8582, Part VII, column (c), list any activity, including one with no 2025 K-1 or Schedule E?" Then collect those carryovers by activity.

findings.who: A shareholder whose 2024 return was prepared by a paid preparer or by software. The filer kept only the Form 1040 and Schedule E, never saw Form 8582, or does not recognize 'passive activity rules' as describing a loss limitation.
findings.why_no: The filer cannot find a Form 8582 among their papers, doesn't remember a loss being 'held back', and answers no rather than 'don't know'.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Column (c): "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Ask whether a Form 8582 was filed with the 2024 return, and offer a 'not sure' answer. That answer should direct the filer to get the full 2024 return or account transcript, and to check whether the 2024 Schedule E showed less loss for this corporation than its K-1 reported.

findings.who: A shareholder with a prior-year unallowed commercial revitalization deduction from this corporation's activity, carried on the 2024 Form 8582.
findings.why_no: The carryover is called a 'deduction' (CRD), not a 'loss', so the filer answers no to a question about a loss being held back.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Line 3: "If you have prior-year unallowed commercial revitalization deductions (CRD) from rental real estate activities, treat that dollar amount as negative..."; Part V: "If you have prior-year unallowed CRD from passive activities other than rental real estate activities, include that amount in Part V."
findings.fix: Add to the help text: "Include any prior-year unallowed commercial revitalization deduction (CRD) for this corporation."

locators: p. 10, Column (c), "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity"

findings.who: A married filer who did not personally work in the S corporation, but whose spouse worked more than 100 and not more than 500 hours in it with no one else, employees or owners, working more, whether they file jointly or separately.
findings.why_no: The gate's first helper asks only whether 'you' worked in the business; it omits 'or your spouse' even though the gated question expressly includes the spouse and the IRS counts the spouse's work. The filer truthfully answers no for themselves, so the gate is false.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through an S corporation ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Change the gate to ask whether you or your spouse worked in the business, and use combined spousal hours for the under-500 and >500 branches.

findings.who: A shareholder who worked more than 100 hours in the S corporation activity with no one else working more, but whose K-1 box 1 is zero or blank—for example, the activity's income is in box 2 or only separately stated items are present.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed as false unless box 1 'shows an amount,' so the tool never asks about the work. Material participation is factual and does not depend on box 1 having ordinary business income.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the corporation' and the standards are based on participation.
findings.fix: Ask the participation question based on work in the activity, not on box 1; use box 1 at most to prioritize, not to gate material participation.

findings.who: A shareholder in an S corporation with more than one activity who worked 600 hours total, including 150 hours in activity A with no one else in activity A working more; or who worked 150 hours in activity A while someone else worked more in activity B.
findings.why_no: The gate and gated question ask about 'this S corporation' and compare hours for the corporation as a whole. The filer reads 'more than 500 hours' as total corporation hours, or 'no one else working more' as across the corporation, and answers no, although test 3 is met for activity A.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the corporation' and 'Each interest in rental real estate is a separate activity, unless you elect to treat all interests in rental real estate as one activity.'
findings.fix: Ask and compute material participation separately for each activity identified on the K-1 statement, not once for the S corporation as a whole.

findings.who: A shareholder in an S corporation with a fiscal tax year ending in 2025 who worked more than 100 hours with no one else working more during that fiscal year, but not during calendar 2025.
findings.why_no: They answer no to 'in 2025' because they did not work in calendar 2025. The material-participation test uses the corporation's tax year, which can include 2024 for a fiscal-year corporation.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'All determinations of material participation are based on your participation during the corporation’s tax year.'
findings.fix: Replace 'in 2025' with 'during the corporation's tax year'.

findings.who: A married filer and spouse who together worked 120 hours in the S corporation with no one else working more, but neither individually worked more than 100 hours.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether 'you (or your spouse)' worked more than 100 hours; the filer reads this as either one individually, not their combined hours, and answers no. The help says to compare 'your hours (with your spouse's)' but does not clearly say to add them to meet the 100-hour threshold.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through an S corporation ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Ask whether you and your spouse together worked more than 100 hours, and state that the hours are combined for the threshold and the comparison.

locators: p. 4, Individuals, "You participated in the activity for more than 100 hours during the tax year, and your participation in the activity for the tax year wasn’t less than the participation in the activity of any other individual"

p. 4, Material participation, "Material participation standards for shareholders who are individuals are listed below"; p. 4, Individuals, "You participated in the activity for more than 500 hours during the tax year"

findings.who: A shareholder in an S corporation with a fiscal tax year beginning in 2025 and ending in 2026, who performed more than 500 hours in the January-June 2026 portion of that tax year but not in calendar 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate and question ask whether they worked 'in 2025'; they truthfully say no because their more-than-500 hours were in 2026, even though those hours are in the corporation's 2025 tax year.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'All determinations of material participation are based on your participation during the corporation’s tax year.'
findings.fix: Ask about the corporation's tax year shown on the Schedule K-1, not calendar 2025; e.g., 'during the corporation's tax year' and count hours in that period.

findings.who: A real-estate-professional shareholder in an S corporation whose box 1 is zero or blank but whose box 2 rental real estate activity has a loss or passive credit, and who worked more than 500 hours in that rental activity in the corporation's tax year.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed only when box 1 shows an amount; because box 1 is zero or blank, the tool never asks and treats more-than-500-hours as false, even though the shareholder's work was in a rental real estate activity held through the S corporation.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: material participation is determined 'in each trade or business activity held through the corporation; and (b) if you were a real estate professional ... in each rental real estate activity held through the corporation'; 'any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through an S corporation ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Gate on any activity of the S corporation for which material participation can matter, including box 2 rental real estate and passive credits, not only on box 1 having an amount.

findings.who: A shareholder who performed more than 500 hours for a partnership or other lower-tier activity owned by the S corporation, but not directly for the S corporation itself.
findings.why_no: They read 'worked in the corporation's business' as work for the S corporation itself, so they answer no for work done at the lower-tier entity.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through an S corporation ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Ask about work 'in connection with any activity held through this S corporation, including lower-tier entities' rather than 'in the corporation's business.'

findings.who: A shareholder whose Schedule K-1 box 1 shows income from one S-corporation activity, but who performed more than 500 hours in a different activity held through the same S corporation and did not work in the box 1 activity.
findings.why_no: They read 'worked in the corporation's business' as the business that produced box 1 income, so they answer no; the question does not say material participation is tested separately for each activity.
findings.irs_text: i1120ssk p. 4: 'You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the corporation; and (b) if you were a real estate professional ... in each rental real estate activity held through the corporation.'
findings.fix: Ask about work in each activity held through the S corporation, or say 'any activity held through this S corporation,' and explain that material participation is tested per activity.

locators: p. 4, Material participation, "Material participation standards for shareholders who are individuals are listed below"; p. 4, Individuals, "You participated in the activity for more than 500 hours during the tax year"

p. 4, Work counted toward material participation, "Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through an S corporation (where you own your stock at the time the work is done) is counted toward material participation"
